title: Model pin bumps must keep old models registered so persisted review arms still resolve
answers: How do I bump the ReviewHog review model?
Why did an in-flight review change model after a model bump?
What happens to persisted review arm when a model is removed from the task catalog?
body:
Each ReviewReport persists its review arm (adapter/model/effort/permission mode) at creation and keeps it for the report's life.
`resolve_review_arm` in products/review_hog/backend/reviewer/constants.py honors a persisted arm only while it is a registry-supported combo; otherwise it falls back to DEFAULT_REVIEW_ARM and stamps `review_arm_fallback`.
So when changing REVIEW_MODEL / FLASH_ARM / VALIDATION_MODEL, do NOT deregister the old model or narrow its supported efforts in the task catalog: in-flight reports would silently jump to the new default (a cheap-tier `low` report would be lifted to full-strength xhigh, costing money).
Products/review_hog/backend/reviewer/tests/test_constants.py covers this with `_LEGACY_CODEX_ARM` params (legacy xhigh and legacy low cheap-tier); keep or extend them on the next bump.
applies: Any change to review/validation model pins or the task-catalog registration of models used by ReviewHog.

search: Model pin changes must keep old models registered because persisted ReviewReport review arms resolve through `resolve_review_arm` in products/review_hog/backend/reviewer/constants.py, which falls back to DEFAULT_REVIEW_ARM and stamps `review_arm_fallback` when a persisted arm becomes unsupported. Deregistering an old model or narrowing its supported efforts silently upgrades in-flight reports to the new default, risking cost overruns (cheap-tier low efforts become xhigh). Keep or extend legacy test params like `_LEGACY_CODEX_ARM` in products/review_hog/backend/reviewer/tests/test_constants.py with each model pin change. Applies to any change of REVIEW_MODEL, FLASH_ARM, VALIDATION_MODEL pins or task-catalog registration of ReviewHog models.
